mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR are simultaneously above their respective all-prior means for the same team; measure corner kicks FOR in those matches versus matches where only one or neither is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick production rises when both shots and shots-on-target are jointly elevated above baseline, more than when only one is elevated — a super-additive joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume (shots FOR) and shots-on-target jointly condition corner kick generation: when a team produces high shot volume alongside a high shots-on-target rate, corner kick production rises disproportionately relative to what either observable alone would predict. Team B's recent surge in both shots (17.0 recent vs 12.4 all-prior) and shots-on-target (6.4 recent vs 5.8 all-prior) should be jointly tested against their corner kick production (6.2 recent vs 4.8 all-prior) to determine whether the joint elevation of both shooting observables predicts corner kick output beyond what each observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables simultaneously (shots AND shots_on_target both elevated), which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. The engine's covered class handles each observable independently against one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team A, condition on matches where shots_on_target FOR is below the all-prior mean while shots FOR is also below the all-prior mean, versus matches where only one is below. Measure goals FOR in each regime.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals FOR are more suppressed when both shot volume and shot accuracy are jointly below baseline than when only one is depressed — the joint deficit is a stronger suppressor than either alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target FOR has dropped sharply in recent matches (2.8 recent vs 4.6 all-prior) while their shots FOR has also declined (9.4 recent vs 10.7 all-prior), but the ratio of shots-on-target to shots (conversion accuracy) may have changed non-proportionally. The joint relationship between shot volume and shot accuracy (shots_on_target / shots ratio) should be tested against goal output to determine whether accuracy decline is a stronger suppressor of goals than volume decline alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneous conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) to capture the joint accuracy-volume interaction on goals. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Cross-condition Team B's goals FOR by half (first vs second) against Team A's goals AGAINST by half (first vs second). Measure whether the combination of Team B's second-half attacking strength and Team A's second-half defensive weakness produces a joint elevation in second-half goals beyond what each team's individual half-split would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals in the match rise when the attacking team has a back-loaded goal production profile and the defending team has a back-loaded goals-conceded profile — the asymmetric half-split interaction amplifies second-half scoring.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a pronounced first-half vs second-half goal asymmetry (1.084 goals FOR in first half vs 1.337 in second half all-prior), while Team A's goal production is more evenly split (0.764 first half vs 0.742 second half). The within-match half-level split of goals FOR for each team should be jointly tested against the opponent's half-level goals AGAINST split to determine whether Team B's second-half goal surge is amplified or suppressed when facing a team (Team A) whose defensive vulnerability is also back-loaded (0.640 goals AGAINST first half vs 0.719 second half).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split that simultaneously conditions on two teams' asymmetric half-level profiles for different observables (goals FOR for one team, goals AGAINST for the other). It is not a single observable with one band, and it requires half-resolution data.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, condition on matches where fouls FOR exceeds a threshold (e.g., above the all-prior mean of 11.6) and measure cards_2h FOR in those matches versus matches below the threshold. Test whether the relationship is non-linear (cards_2h rises sharply only above the foul threshold).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) rises non-linearly with foul volume — suppressed at low foul counts but surging beyond a threshold foul level, rather than increasing proportionally across the full range.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's cards_2h FOR (1.684 per second half) is notably higher than their cards_2h AGAINST (1.211), and both exceed the competition context mean (1.378). The within-match second-half card accumulation for Team B should be jointly tested against their fouls FOR (which has risen recently to 12.8 vs 11.6 all-prior) to determine whether high foul volume in a match is a threshold predictor of elevated second-half card accumulation — i.e., whether there is a non-linear relationship where second-half cards surge once foul volume crosses a threshold.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a threshold/non-linear dependence of one observable (cards_2h) on a continuous second observable (fouls), conditioned within a specific match period (second half). It is not a single observable with one coarse band, and it requires half-resolution data for cards_2h.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's possession FOR exceeds a threshold (above competition mean of 50%) AND the opponent's corner_kicks AGAINST is above the competition mean (5.0 per match). Measure Team B's corner_kicks FOR in those jointly-conditioned matches versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick production for the possession-dominant team rises when both possession dominance and opponent corner-concession propensity are jointly present, more than when either condition holds alone — an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B holds dominant possession (55.9% all-prior, 54.0% recent) while Team A is near-neutral (50.2% all-prior, 54.2% recent). The asymmetric possession relationship between the two teams should be jointly tested against corner kick differential: when one team holds structurally higher possession AND the opponent allows above-average corners (Team A allows 4.0 corners per match all-prior), the possession-dominant team's corner production should be elevated beyond what possession alone or corner-allowed alone would predict. This tests whether possession dominance and opponent corner-concession jointly amplify corner generation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric relationship across different observables for the two sides (Team B's possession FOR jointly with Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single observable with one band. It requires conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously.
